info.title: pipwerk replay
info.description: Web API of pipwerk replay, version 1: the test accounts and the data stock of historical price data (list of series, details, brokers, import of several files, completeness). Data come into the data stock only through the import. The paths below /api/v1/ are versioned; the technical endpoint /api/health and the internal endpoints below /api/replay/ (settings, revision) are not part of this description.

get.summary: List the series of the data stock
get.description: Lists the rows of the data stock page by page: one row per broker, instrument and data (candles of a time unit, ticks, or - for an instrument that has instrument data and no series - the instrument data, ``contract``), with the first and the last moment and the number of gaps. The filters ``broker``, ``instrument`` and ``data`` each match a part of the text without regard to case; a filter that no row matches (for example an unknown identifier of data) gives an empty list. ``total`` counts all rows that match. The rows are sorted by broker, instrument and data (time units from short to long, then ticks, then contract). ``limit`` is at most ``max_listed_items`` (default 1000).

post.summary: Import several files in one process
post.description: Imports any number of files (at most ``max_files_per_import``, default 100; together at most ``max_import_bytes``, default 256 MiB; each at most ``max_upload_bytes``, default 32 MiB and ``max_rows`` rows, default 500 000). The body is a ``multipart/form-data`` form: ``broker`` once for all files (it also replaces the broker named in a JSON file), ``timezone`` once for all CSV files, and the parts ``file``; optionally ``instrument`` and ``data`` once per file in the order of the files (an empty value for none). JSON files (JSON format of ``contracts/market-data/v1/``, candles, ticks or instrument data) name instrument and data in their content; a given ``instrument`` replaces the one of the content, a given ``data`` must equal the one of the content. CSV files (export format of MetaTrader 5, candles or ticks) need ``instrument`` and ``data`` (a time unit or ``ticks``). Every file is taken over in a transaction of its own; rows of the same time replace those that exist; rows that fail the checks are rejected and named with a reason. A file that is refused as a whole (wrong format, nothing readable, unknown time zone, missing or unknown data) changes nothing and does not stop the others: the answer (HTTP 200) has a result per file, in the order of the files. HTTP 422 if the form is wrong or has no file, HTTP 413 if there are too many files or they are too large together, HTTP 403 if a web page of another origin sends the form (the header ``Origin`` is not the address of the backend).

post.summary: Read what files say about themselves
post.description: For the dialog of the import: tells for each file, without importing anything, its format (``json`` or ``csv``), and the broker, instrument and data it names. A JSON file names them in its content; a CSV file in its name, as far as the name follows ``<Instrument>_<Data>_<from>_<to>`` (the export of MetaTrader 5 and the files meant for the import, for example ``EURUSD_H1_202301020000_202312292300.csv``) or ``<Instrument>,<Data>`` (also with ``_`` or a space, for example ``EURUSD,H1.csv``), with ``<Data>`` a time unit, ``TICKS`` or ``CONTRACT``, without regard to case. The content of a CSV file is not read, so the client may send it empty. ``broker`` of the answer is the broker that all JSON files name (``null`` if there is none, or they name none or different ones). The form is that of the import, with the parts ``file`` only; the limits are those of the import.

post.description: For every needed part (candles of a time unit or ticks of an instrument in a period, or the data of an instrument) tells what is needed, what is present and what is missing, in the order of the request. The broker is the broker for test runs unless the request names one (HTTP 409 if the data stock has no broker at all). At most ``max_parts_per_request`` parts (default 100).

FileHint.title: FileHint
FileHint.description:
What the backend recognizes about one file without importing it.

``format`` is ``json`` or ``csv`` (from the extension of the name, else from the first
character of the content). ``instrument`` and ``data`` come from the content of a JSON file,
else from the name; ``data`` is a time unit (``m1`` to ``mn1``), ``ticks`` or ``contract``.
``broker`` is the broker a JSON file names (``null`` for CSV). A value that the file does
not name is ``null``. ``error`` is set if a JSON file cannot be read.

FileOutcome.title: FileOutcome
FileOutcome.description:
The result for one file of an import, in the order of the files of the request.

Either ``result`` is set (the file was taken over; single rows may be rejected, see
``result``) or ``error`` and ``message`` (the whole file is refused and nothing of it was
changed). ``refused`` tells which. ``name`` is the name of the file without a directory.
``message`` is a fixed text that names fields, never content of the file.

ImportOutcome.title: ImportOutcome
ImportOutcome.description:
The result of an import of several files. A refused file does not stop the others.
``imported_count`` counts the files that were taken over, ``refused_count`` those that
were refused.

ImportPreview.title: ImportPreview
ImportPreview.description:
The hints for the dialog of an import, one per file in the order of the request.

``broker`` is the broker that all JSON files name, ``null`` if there is no JSON file, one of
them names none or they name different ones.

ImportRefused.title: ImportRefused
ImportRefused.description:
Error body for an import that is refused as a whole (nothing was read or changed): no
file (HTTP 422), more files than ``max_files_per_import`` or larger together than
``max_import_bytes`` (HTTP 413). ``message`` is a fixed text.

ImportResult.title: ImportResult
ImportResult.description:
The result of an import.

``accepted`` counts the rows taken over, ``replaced`` those of them that replaced an existing
row of the same moment. ``rejected`` lists at most the first ``max_reported_rejections``
rejected rows; ``rejected_count`` counts all. ``period_start`` and ``period_end`` span the rows
taken over (``null`` if there are none).

InstrumentInfo.title: InstrumentInfo
InstrumentInfo.description: The newest data of an instrument at a broker (``contracts/market-data/v1/``).

InstrumentPart.title: InstrumentPart
InstrumentPart.description: The details of one instrument (no period).

InvalidRequest.title: InvalidRequest
InvalidRequest.description:
Error body for a request or body that does not fit the schema (HTTP 422). Names
at most 50 places and the error type of each, never the values.

MissingPeriod.title: MissingPeriod
MissingPeriod.description: A missing period and why it is missing.

MissingReason.title: MissingReason
MissingReason.description: Why part of a period is missing.

PartCompleteness.title: PartCompleteness
PartCompleteness.description:
One needed part: what is needed, what is present, what is missing.

For candles and ticks ``present`` and ``missing`` split the needed period (times in which
the market is closed count as present); ``complete`` is true if nothing is missing. For
``instrument`` both lists are empty and ``complete`` tells whether data exist. The lists hold
at most ``max_listed_items`` periods, the counts count all of them.

RejectReason.title: RejectReason
RejectReason.description: Why a row of an import file was rejected.

RejectedRow.title: RejectedRow
RejectedRow.description:
A rejected row: the line number in a CSV file (the header is line 1), the position of
the entry in a JSON file, and why.

SeriesDetails.title: SeriesDetails
SeriesDetails.description:
The details of one row of the list: the gaps and the instrument data.

``gaps`` lists at most ``max_listed_items`` gaps in time order; ``row.gap_count`` counts all
of them. A gap lies within the covered periods and within the trading time. ``contract`` is
the newest instrument data of the instrument at this broker, ``null`` if there are none (the
data are missing, and a test run does not start without them).

SeriesPage.title: SeriesPage
SeriesPage.description:
A page of the list of series, sorted by broker, instrument and data (time units from short
to long, then ticks, then contract). ``total`` counts all rows that match the filters.

SeriesRow.title: SeriesRow
SeriesRow.description:
One row of the list: the candles of one time unit, the ticks, or - only for an instrument
that has instrument data but no series - the instrument data (``data`` is ``contract``).

``first`` and ``last`` are the moments of the first and the last candle or tick (UTC);
``null`` for ``contract``. ``gap_count`` counts the gaps over the covered range of the
series; 0 for ``contract``.
